# 2 Baruch Chapter 34 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 2 Baruch Chapter 34 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 34:2 — "dismayed / shattered"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Why-are-you-dismayed" | Syriac: troubled/disturbed |
| LOGOS | "Why are you dismayed" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "Why are you so shattered" | Stronger emotional term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "dismayed" (EMET/LOGOS). "Shattered" overstates; the Syriac term is more moderate.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 34:3 — "brings forth its own portion / produces what belongs to it"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "every-age brings-forth its-own-[portion]" | Literal birth/produce verb |
| LOGOS | "every age brings forth its own portion" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "every age produces what belongs to it" | Functional paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "brings forth its own portion." The birth metaphor in "brings forth" mirrors the agricultural imagery of the verse and is more vivid than PNEUMA's flat "produces."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
